newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Jan trade deficit falls to $150 mln.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Jan trade deficit falls to $150 mln.

text.p: Peru's trade deficit was $150 million in January, 21 percent lower than the $190 million in the same month last year, the Central Reserve Bank said Friday.

Exports grew 24 percent in January to $551 million from $443 million in the same month last year, the bank said. Meanwhile, January imports rose 11 percent to $700 million, compared with $633 million in January 1996, the bank said in its weekly report.

Peru's traditional export sectors of minerals, oil, agriculture and fishing grew 17 percent in January to $382 million. The fastest growing traditional export sector was fishing, which rose 102 percent to $128 million.
Non-traditional exports grew by 53 percent to $163 million from $106 million.
